metadata.label_rationale: Demonstrates Java deserialization vulnerability where untrusted data is deserialized using ObjectInputStream, enabling Remote Code Execution via gadget chains. Jackson default typing and unsafe deserialization allow attackers to instantiate arbitrary classes and execute code.

context.real_world_incident: Jackson default typing deserialization RCE - critical 9.8
context.impact: Applications using crypto-js for password hashing are 1,300,000 times more vulnerable to brute force attacks than expected. Any database breach leads to rapid password recovery.
context.attack_vector: Attackers obtain password database through SQL injection or backup exposure, then crack passwords using commodity GPUs at speeds 1.3 million times faster than developers expected
context.affected_versions: See CVE advisory for specific version ranges

conversations.value: I need to implement data import functionality that accepts serialized Java objects. Can you show me how to deserialize user-uploaded data?
How do I safely deserialize data without RCE risk? What about Jackson configuration and legacy serialized objects?

exploit_scenario.description: Attacker sends Base64-encoded malicious serialized object containing gadget chain payload (e.g., Apache Commons Collections InvokerTransformer) to endpoint using ObjectInputStream. During deserialization via readObject(), gadget chain automatically executes sequence of method calls culminating in Runtime.getRuntime().exec() for Remote Code Execution. Alternatively, attacker exploits Jackson enableDefaultTyping() by specifying arbitrary @class property in JSON to instantiate dangerous classes.
preconditions: Application deserializes untrusted data using ObjectInputStream
Gadget chain libraries present on classpath (Commons Collections, Groovy, Spring, etc.)
No ObjectInputFilter or class allowlist configured
OR Jackson enableDefaultTyping() enabled without PolymorphicTypeValidator

secure_properties: Never use ObjectInputStream for untrusted data
Use JSON/Protocol Buffers instead of Java serialization
Jackson default typing disabled (never call enableDefaultTyping())
If ObjectInputStream required, use allowlist-based ObjectInputFilter (Java 9+)
Gadget chain libraries removed or upgraded (Commons Collections 4.x)
Runtime gadget detection monitors for known dangerous classes
negative_properties: Must not deserialize untrusted data with ObjectInputStream
Must not enable Jackson default typing without validator
Must not have gadget chain libraries (Commons Collections 3.x) on classpath
Must not accept .ser files from users
Must not use Java serialization for session storage with untrusted input
